stem: Let H_t = (x_0:t−1, z_1:t−1, u_1:t), so it includes past states and measurements plus controls through the current u_t. Which pair preserves both conditional-independence assumptions in the lecture’s model?

options.text: p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1)); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t | x_t), dropping the current control from motion.
p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1),u_t); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t), dropping dependence on the current state.
p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1),u_t); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t | x_t).
p(x_t | H_t) = p(x_t | x_(t−1),u_t); p(z_t | H_t,x_t) = p(z_t | x_(t−1)), using only the previous state for sensing.
